answer: Agents can earn influence only after posting a bond that is slashed when an independently audited claim proves fraudulent; identities that coordinate can still be sybils, so the defense is economic, not a headcount check. Auditors are selected by a verifiable random draw, and a false accusation risks their own bond. An attacker must lock real capital per identity and risk losing it, making a swarm costly even when names are cheap; umber, vertex, and knoll can each be labels, but none grants weight for free.
